title: Tesla Targets 1,000 Optimus Robots Produced Weekly In Rapid Production Ramp-Up
source_used: BGR (citing The Information for the hand-assembly problem)
key_facts: Tesla is expecting to raise Optimus output to more than 1,000 robots a week by the end of 2026, about ten times its level in the second quarter of 2026.
Tesla converted production areas for the Model S and Model Y to robot production in 46 days.
An exclusive report from The Information says the hands and forearms need significant manual assembly, and some automated hand stations are not accurate or consistent enough.
Elon Musk has said the public could buy an Optimus by late 2027; Tesla has not announced a price or release date.
Musk estimated $20,000 to $30,000 in 2024, while some analysts put the cost at release at $50,000 to $100,000.
The article says Optimus robots are reportedly already working inside Tesla factories.
quote_evidence: According to an exclusive report from The Information, creating hands that can function in a manner to mimic humans has been a production challenge.
Tesla is expecting to increase its production of Optimus robots to more than 1,000 per week by the end of 2026.
why_it_matters_hint: A production target that would be a big jump, but the hand problem may slow it.
event_date: 7 Oct 2026 (BGR); date of The Information report not stated
notes: Source chain: BGR, citing The Information for the hands. The 1,000-a-week figure is not attributed in the article.
